a: Bandwidth is capacity (bits/sec); latency is delay (time).
Throughput is actual successful data transfer rate.
RTT is round-trip time — time for a signal to go and acknowledgment to return.
MTU is maximum transmission unit — largest packet size for a link.
TCP window controls how much data can be in flight before ACK.
Congestion control slows senders when the network is overloaded.
Packet loss drops data in transit; TCP retransmits, UDP does not.
Jitter is variation in packet delay — harmful for voice/video.
QoS prioritizes certain traffic types for better service quality.
Anycast routes a request to the nearest or best of several destinations sharing an IP.
